corrections.form_value: With N = 35 in a within-subjects AUT design, persistent AI raised mean originality only for semantically rich objects, flexible AI did not raise mean originality, and both AI conditions raised initial originality (abstract, OpenAlex record; no numbers in the abstract).
corrections.source_says: The abstract says that, for semantically sparse tasks, a tentative temporal originality benefit from flexible AI was not evident in overall mean originality. It does not state a flexible-AI mean-originality result for semantically rich tasks, so the unqualified claim that flexible AI did not raise mean originality exceeds this source. Use "no overall mean-originality benefit was evident for flexible AI on semantically sparse tasks" and replace "no numbers in the abstract" with "no numeric effect estimates or inferential statistics in the abstract", because N = 35 is reported.
corrections.quote: For semantically sparse tasks, these analyses provided tentative evidence of an originality benefit from flexible AI, but this pattern was not evident in overall mean originality.
corrections.locator: OpenAlex W7204213697, complete abstract reconstructed from abstract_inverted_index, checked 2026-10-09 (https://api.openalex.org/works/https://doi.org/10.1080/10400419.2026.2721513); sentence 7 for the flexible-AI finding; sentence 3 for N = 35.

confirmed: Source checked: the complete OpenAlex abstract and Crossref/Semantic Scholar metadata, not the journal full text. retrieval.json[c086] has status not_obtained; OpenAlex open_access reports closed access and no repository full text; Semantic Scholar openAccessPdf reports CLOSED; the publisher full-text URL returned HTTP 403. No PDF, markdown full text, or appendices were available for this check (OpenAlex W7204213697; Crossref DOI 10.1080/10400419.2026.2721513; Semantic Scholar d97dba341a55d776d2f4ec9edf3b06d9a562426c; checked 2026-10-09).

The title and authors Zheng Liang, Jie Shen, and Dan Zhang match the metadata; Creativity Research Journal, online publication 2026-08-25, and page range 1-20 are confirmed. The form correctly identifies its evidentiary source as abstract only; the page range is metadata, not a verified PDF page count (Crossref title, author, container-title, published-online, page, and link.content-version; https://api.crossref.org/works/10.1080%2F10400419.2026.2721513).

The described study uses a within-subjects Alternative Uses Task with semantically rich and sparse objects under flexible AI, persistent AI, and a no-AI baseline. This is human AI assistance with output originality outcomes, not a synthesis or a comparison solely of AI-generated versus human-generated output (OpenAlex abstract, sentences 1-7).

N = 35 refers to participants, not ideas or ratings, and is below the 50-person eligibility threshold. The abstract does not distinguish recruitment, assignment, and analysis counts or describe exclusions; retaining null for n_randomized and n_analyzed avoids inventing those counts (OpenAlex abstract, sentence 3; creativity-codebook.md, section 3).

Randomized condition order and counterbalancing are not stated anywhere in the complete abstract. design_class = other, assignment.randomized = not_stated, and criterion_1_random_assignment_of_ai = unclear are appropriate for this limited source; has_randomized_people_study = false means no randomized people study could be confirmed, not that nonrandom assignment was established (OpenAlex abstract, especially sentence 3; creativity-codebook.md, sections 3-4).

Core eligibility = no and context_class = none are supported by the reported small human-assistance experiment and the absence of evidence establishing an observational, synthesis, or AI-versus-human-output design; this remains an abstract-only classification (OpenAlex abstract, sentences 2-7; creativity-codebook.md, section 3).

Flexible assistance promotes cross-category exploration and persistent assistance promotes within-category deepening; AI supplies tailored cues after each participant idea. The abstract does not identify the model, participant population, task duration, originality-scoring method, or analysis unit, so those details cannot be filled from this source (OpenAlex abstract, sentences 2-4 and complete abstract).

S1-O1 reported quotation is verbatim: persistent AI significantly increased mean originality only for semantically rich tasks. No effect estimate, confidence interval, p value, or test statistic accompanies it (OpenAlex abstract, sentence 5).

S1-O2 reported quotation is verbatim and its prose correctly restricts the tentative temporal benefit, absent in overall mean originality, to semantically sparse tasks (OpenAlex abstract, sentence 7).

S1-O3 reported quotation is verbatim: both flexible and persistent AI elevated initial originality across both task types relative to baseline, with a slower subsequent increase. No numeric result statistics accompany this finding (OpenAlex abstract, sentence 6).

The abstract reports an empirical experiment and provides no synthesis study count, pooled effect, interval, or standardizer; leaving the synthesis fields at their defaults is appropriate (OpenAlex abstract, complete text).
summary: The complete OpenAlex abstract describes a within-subjects AUT study with N = 35, but does not establish randomization or distinguish recruited from analyzed participants. The small-study exclusion is supported, but the one-line finding should restrict the flexible-AI mean-originality statement to semantically sparse tasks and specify that numeric effect estimates, rather than all numbers, are absent.
